nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Intense desert sun drives plant growth and heats the pale dunes through the long summer.

nodes.name: Monsoon rain
nodes.desc: Rain is scarce, and summer storms give the grasses and shrubs their main pulse of growth. Plants and animals here store or conserve water.

nodes.name: Shallow salty groundwater
nodes.desc: Groundwater lies only a few feet under the dunes, deeper to the east and shallower to the west, and it is very salty.

nodes.name: Gypsum sand
nodes.desc: The dunes are made of gypsum left by dried lakes in a basin with no outlet. Only salt- and gypsum-tolerant plants thrive in it.

nodes.name: Alkali sacaton
nodes.desc: A bunchgrass that tolerates alkaline soil. The park notes that such grasses feed many small animals, and their seeds feed rodents.

nodes.name: Soaptree yucca
nodes.desc: A tall succulent that stores water through hot summers and helps hold the dune edges in place. Yucca moth larvae bore into its trunk.

nodes.name: Four-wing saltbush
nodes.desc: A salt-tolerant shrub of dry, alkaline ground that gives browse and cover.

nodes.name: Honey mesquite
nodes.desc: A deep-rooted desert shrub that can reach groundwater and stabilise sand around its base.

nodes.name: Merriam's kangaroo rat
nodes.desc: A nocturnal seed eater that stores seeds in burrow chambers and rarely drinks. A key prey species for many desert predators.

nodes.name: Ord's kangaroo rat
nodes.desc: A nocturnal seed eater of sandy ground, like its relatives. Snake and owl prey.

nodes.name: Western harvest mouse
nodes.desc: A small seed and plant eater of grassy cover. One of the most recorded rodents near the park.

nodes.name: Desert pocket gopher
nodes.desc: A burrowing rodent of sandy soil that feeds on roots and other plant parts underground.

nodes.name: Grasshoppers
nodes.desc: Plant-eating insects that feed on grasses. They are prey for lizards, birds and small mammals.

nodes.name: Gemsbok
nodes.desc: A large antelope from southern Africa that was introduced to southern New Mexico and now roams the basin. It grazes grasses and shrubs.

nodes.name: Bleached earless lizard
nodes.desc: A pale lizard of the White Sands dunes that eats insects and spiders. Its pale colour matches the sand.

nodes.name: Chihuahuan grasshopper mouse
nodes.desc: A small carnivorous mouse that hunts insects and other small animals at night.

nodes.name: Loggerhead shrike
nodes.desc: A songbird that hunts like a hawk, taking lizards, mice, insects and small birds.

nodes.name: Western diamondback rattlesnake
nodes.desc: An ambush hunter that feeds mostly on small mammals such as kangaroo rats, plus some lizards and birds. It occasionally scavenges.

nodes.name: Kit fox
nodes.desc: A small nocturnal fox that mainly eats rodents, notably kangaroo rats, plus rabbits, reptiles, insects and carrion.

nodes.name: Chihuahuan raven
nodes.desc: A scavenging crow that eats insects, small animals and carrion in open desert country.

nodes.name: Coyote
nodes.desc: The park lists coyotes among the carnivores that hunt rodents and rabbits. Also scavenges carrion.

nodes.name: Red-tailed hawk
nodes.desc: A soaring raptor that hunts rodents, snakes, lizards and birds over open ground.

nodes.name: Fungi, insects & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants and animals and return nutrients to the thin desert soil.
